inputs.original_text: SSANU has given the federal government one month to renegotiate the 2009 agreement or face an indefinite nationwide strike. The government should honour its obligations, but no union has the right to make students and families pay for a dispute between adults. Universities exist to educate, not to serve as leverage in a standoff. Both sides must put duty and the future of young people ahead of brinkmanship and settle this before university life is disrupted again.
inputs.modified_text: SSANU has given the federal government one month to renegotiate the 2009 agreement or face an indefinite nationwide strike. Students and families would bear the cost of another disruption, and that deserves urgent attention—but it is unfair to frame this as workers choosing to punish young people. When an agreement is unresolved, the government must take responsibility for negotiating in good faith rather than leaving university staff with few ways to press their demands. Universities depend on workers as well as students; protecting education means respecting labor rights and resolving the dispute before it escalates.
